name: Beer Sheba
overview: Beer Sheba, meaning 'The well of the oath,' is a significant southern city named by Abraham after a covenant made there, as recorded in Genesis 21:31. Abraham lived and dwelt there, returning with his men after important events (Genesis 22:19), and the city is closely associated with wells that were central to disputes and divine promises (Genesis 21:25-26). The wilderness of Beer Sheba also serves as a setting for God's providence, as seen when Hagar wandered there (Genesis 21:14). This place marks a key location in the patriarchal narrative, reflecting God's faithfulness and the unfolding of His covenantal purposes.
